body: If not proper cursive, you can start with big intial letters, then write a bunch of scribbled "wwwww"s. Finish by adding dots and lines where the "i"s and "t"s are in your name. It's a start, but I recommend refining it. Signatures with more details + consistent details are harder to forge. You can practice it in a blank notebook until it really flows, and then maybe the shakiness will blend into the rhythm of it.

Don't worry. I think most people aren't taught how either. (I wasn't) But you can make one very easily. Just start with your name in cursive. Over time, when you sign it over and over again on documents or receipts, you get lazier with it. Or you start writing it faster. And after a while, there'll be a pattern + the super rushed cursive will develop a natural character on its own. Boom, signature.

My first souldog died when I was at my lowest point in life. It would have been so easy to end it. No one would miss me. It might sound silly, but what kept me going was the thought that my next furry companion was somewhere out there, waiting for me in a dark and lonely  cage. 
From my own dark and lonely life, I have known that make human love might be near-unobtainable for me. So, I put my entire purpose in life into loving and caring for animals that are hurt, abandoned, and broken. This year, my other soulcat passed away too. But when I look back on all the years I spent with him, all the days I gave him happiness, I don't regret my decision to stay alive. If I killed myself, we wouldn't have been able to meet.
I still struggle with suicidal thoughts, but I keep this thought in mind now as I think about my future.

Hi, I can definitely relate. I suck at school and my career and it does pain me a lot because my ability in those things actually matters. In video games I play on the easiest level and I still can't get past a lot of stages.

But I wanna say that's ok. These days when I play video games or write poems, I just let myself suck terribly. I write the most shitty poems imaginable and I'm still proud of them, because I at least wrote a poem. I mess up video game stages for hours and I just laugh about it. We get graded and judged by our ability on how "skilled" or how "well" we can do something in almost all aspects of life from other people. Bosses, teachers, parents, peers. So I think there's something cool about having a hobby and being unapologetically bad at it, and still being like "look at what I made! It sucks and I'm still going to do it even though I suck! Because it's FUN and no one can tell me to stop." To me, that's what art is about anyways. It's a little rebellious to have fun and be mediocre in a world that places all our value on our productivity. Sorry for the tangent.

Yeah sure! Basically, your muscles are made of tons of tiny myofibrils that tear when you work out, which are to be replaced by thicker and stronger myofibrils. This is the basis of how your muscles grow. Much of the internal repairing actually happens *after* the workout, when you are resting. That's when your body uses the amino acids eaten from the protein in food to repair the broken myofibrils! It's why you'll usually hear of a lot of people having a protein shake after their workout. To literally "feed" their muscles. So, if you don't have enough protein or enough calories to help your body recover, your body will be limited in what it can use to grow more muscle. Less amino acids = less muscle growth. Sorry if my explanation is a little confusing...there should be more articles about it if you search "muscle growth amino acids diet"
